scope: Primary human studies informing structured athlete-response inputs and conservative adaptive guardrails. These sources support measurement choices and cautious decision rules; they do not validate Bell as a medical device or guarantee outcomes.

sources.title: Performance and Physiological Effects of Race Pace-Based Versus Heart Rate Variability-Guided Training Prescription in Runners
supports: event-pace, heart-rate, and HRV information can represent distinct endurance-prescription signals
individual response variation should be expected

sources.title: Continued sports activity, using a pain-monitoring model, during rehabilitation in patients with Achilles tendinopathy: a randomized controlled study
supports: pain should be explicitly monitored when training decisions are adjusted
pain-monitoring rules must remain condition- and context-specific

sources.title: Personalizing Resistance Training Mitigates Neuromuscular and Perceived Fatigue: The Autoregulation Cluster Training Method
supports: personalized resistance-training structure can reduce fatigue
completed performance and perceived fatigue are useful together

sources.title: Research application of session-RPE in monitoring the training load of elite endurance athletes
supports: session RPE and actual duration are useful internal-load inputs
planned-versus-actual duration matters when interpreting session load

sources.title: Monitoring load, recovery, and performance in young elite soccer players
supports: training duration, session RPE, recovery, and repeated field performance should be considered longitudinally
frequent performance checks are preferable to one isolated observation

sources.title: Analysing the predictive capacity and dose-response of wellness in load monitoring
supports: wellness responses alone have limited predictive capacity
readiness should not independently drive large prescription changes

sources.title: Heart rate variability in prediction of individual adaptation to endurance training in recreational endurance runners
supports: recovery physiology can add context but should be interpreted with performance data

sources.title: Monitoring Sleep and Nightly Recovery with Wrist-Worn Wearables: Links to Training Load and Performance Adaptations
supports: sleep and nightly recovery can be tracked alongside training load
recovery signals are contextual inputs rather than deterministic prescriptions
